snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹1–3 crore for a product team, doctor network and patient acquisition
snapshot.margin_d2c: Consult fees, subscriptions or care packages of ₹500–20,000 per patient
snapshot.margin_production: Doctor and partner fees usually take 40–70% of the patient fee
snapshot.distribution_note: Patients trust doctors, not apps; partnerships with clinics and hospitals matter most

tailwinds: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission gives every patient a health ID and lets records move between providers.
Telemedicine has been legal under national guidelines since 2020, and patients in smaller towns now use it.
Chronic conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and infertility need long-term care that clinics struggle to provide.
Insurers and employers are paying for preventive and remote care programmes.
headwinds: Large players such as Practo, Tata 1mg, Apollo 24|7 and PharmEasy dominate bookings and pharmacy.
Patients will pay for a doctor, but rarely for an app on its own.
Health data is sensitive, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act adds compliance work.
Many healthtech startups raised money in 2021 and shut down when funding dried up.
angle_2026: Generic doctor booking and medicine delivery are already owned by large companies. The healthtech businesses with a future in 2026 own one condition or one patient journey, such as post-transplant care, fertility or disability, and show measurable outcomes that a patient, insurer or hospital will pay for.
cost_basis: Estimated for a team of 3–5 building a care service for one condition in one or two cities, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: App or web platform, booking, records, payments
Doctor, nutritionist or counsellor fees for the first months
Company setup, privacy policy, data-protection work, doctor agreements
Clinic partnerships, community camps, digital ads

rows: ₹500–2,000 per programme; more when patients renew
unit_economics.note: Renewals and referrals decide whether this works. A patient who renews twice is worth three times as much, at almost no extra acquisition cost.

investor_probes: Who pays: the patient, an employer, an insurer or a hospital?
What outcomes can you show, in numbers?
How much does it cost to win a patient, and how long do they stay?
How do you keep health data safe and compliant?
Why won't a large health platform add this as a feature?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start as a service before building an app. Run the care programme with WhatsApp, a spreadsheet and one doctor, prove patients pay and stay, then build software for what you do every day.
licences: Registered medical practitioners for any consultation, following the Telemedicine Practice Guidelines
Pharmacy licence if you sell medicines
Privacy policy and consent flows under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act
ABDM integration if you handle health records (optional, but useful)

hard_truths.title: Patients pay for care, not software
hard_truths.text: An app nobody is paid to follow up on gets deleted. The revenue sits in the care team, so plan your business around their time.

hard_truths.title: Trust takes years
hard_truths.text: Patients follow their doctor's advice. Partnering with respected doctors or hospitals is slower than ads, but it's what brings patients who stay.

hard_truths.title: Regulation keeps changing
hard_truths.text: Telemedicine, online pharmacy and data rules have all changed in recent years. Budget for a lawyer who knows healthcare.

hard_truths.title: Funding cycles
hard_truths.text: Healthtech funding rose sharply and then fell. Build a business that can survive on its own revenue for long stretches.

plan_goal: The aim is 50 paying patients in one programme, with at least half renewing or completing it.

plan.title: Pick one condition
steps: Choose one condition or patient journey where care breaks down today.
Interview 20 patients or carers and 5 doctors.
Check what they pay for today and what they complain about.

plan.title: Run it by hand
steps: Sign one doctor or clinic as a partner.
Run the programme on WhatsApp and simple forms.
Put consent forms and a privacy policy in place.

plan.title: Get paying patients
steps: Sign up your first 30–50 paying patients through doctors and communities.
Ask every patient what would make them renew.

plan.title: Review
steps: Measure completion, renewals and cost per patient.
Decide which parts to automate first.
Approach an insurer, employer or hospital with your outcome data.
